To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the radiative corrections in the supersymmetric scenario are able to generate a mass hierarchy between atmospheric and solar neutrinos, and that the vacuum oscillation solar neutrino solution is excluded.

in supersymmetric extensions of the Standard Model, radiative corrections can naturally explain why the solar and the atmospheric neutrino mass squared differences are very different, and that in this context, the vacuum oscillations solution of the solar neutrino puzzle is ruled out.

the radiative corrections in the MSSM can naturally accommodate the bimaximal pattern of neutrino masses and mixing if the lightest neutrino is essentially massless and the heaviest neutrino mass is in the 1-10 eV range.

the MSSM with a see-saw neutrino mass matrix is a very promising scenario to explain the observed neutrino masses and mixings.

the MSSM with radiative corrections is consistent with the nearly degenerate neutrino hypothesis and with the atmospheric and large angle MSW solar neutrino oscillation solutions, but is not compatible with the vacuum oscillation scenario.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MSSM with nearly degenerate neutrinos is a viable model for the solution of the neutrino mass puzzle, and that radiative corrections are crucial to obtain the correct neutrino oscillation phenomenology.
the MSSM is consistent with the neutrino oscillation data and with all known experimental constraints.
in the supersymmetric context, the radiative contributions to the light neutrino mass matrix are not negligible, and they can play a relevant role in the determination of the neutrino mass spectrum.
